peers.name: emil-design-eng
peers.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

peers.name: review-animations
peers.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

peers.name: apple-design
peers.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

peers.name: animation-vocabulary
peers.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

en.tagline: Picks a frontend library from a curated list
en.summary: This skill recommends one library for a frontend task. It matches the task to a fixed list that covers UI primitives, toasts, drawers, charts, drag and drop, state, and styling. The user gets a single pick instead of a list of options.
problem: Frontend projects have many libraries for the same job, such as toasts, drawers, or class name helpers. Choosing one takes time, and the choice may not match the project's existing code.

With this skill, the task is matched to a curated list and one library is recommended with a short reason. If the project already uses a different library for that job, the skill flags it but does not change the dependency unless asked.
fit: Choosing a toast, drawer, or command menu library
Picking a chart library for live data or static dashboards
Deciding between clsx and cva for class names
unfit: Tasks outside the curated list, unless you accept general advice
Replacing a library your project already uses
steps: Identify the task the user needs done, not the library they named.
Check `package.json` for a listed library the project already uses.
If the project uses a different library for the same job, flag it and leave the dependency unchanged unless asked.
Match the task to the curated list and recommend one library with a one-sentence purpose.
If the task is not on the list, say so and suggest a library from general knowledge, marked as outside the list.

zh.tagline: 从精选清单中为前端任务挑选库
zh.summary: 这个技能为前端任务推荐一个库。它把任务对应到固定清单上，清单涵盖基础 UI 组件、消息提示、抽屉、图表、拖放、状态管理和样式等类别。用户得到的是一个明确的推荐，而不是一堆选项。
problem: 前端项目里，同一类工作往往有多个库可选，比如消息提示、抽屉或类名工具。挑选需要时间，而且选中的库未必和项目现有代码契合。
使用这个技能后，任务会被对应到精选清单，并给出一个推荐库和简短理由。如果项目已经在该场景使用了其他库，技能会指出来，但除非用户要求，不会改动依赖。
fit: 选择消息提示、抽屉或命令面板库
为实时数据或静态仪表盘挑选图表库
在 clsx 和 cva 之间决定类名处理方式
unfit: 清单之外的任务，除非你接受通用建议
替换项目里已经在用的库
steps: 先确认用户要完成的任务，而不是他提到的库名。
检查 `package.json`，看项目是否已经在用清单中的库。
如果项目在同一场景使用了其他库，指出来，除非用户要求，否则不改动依赖。
把任务对应到精选清单，推荐一个库，并用一句话说明它的用途。
如果任务不在清单中，就直接说明，并基于通用知识给出建议，同时标注它不在清单之内。
